summary:
A bracket must be removed exactly when it has no partner: a `)` that arrives with nothing open, or a `(` never
closed. Matching with a stack (or two counter passes) identifies exactly those, and removing only them is the
minimum. O(n).

question.md:
Remove the fewest brackets so the remaining brackets are balanced; letters stay. Return any valid result.

- **Letters never move or disappear.**
- **Several answers can be valid** (which of two equivalent `)` to drop); any one is accepted.
- **Removing unmatched brackets is enough and necessary:** every unmatched bracket must go, and once they're
  gone the rest is balanced.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Letters are never removed.
- Several minimal answers can exist; any one is accepted.
- Strays can be `)` with nothing open or `(` never closed.

think.md:
**Why a stack.** In a well-formed bracket string, the bracket opened most recently must be closed first: brackets
nest, they never cross. "Most recent first" is exactly last-in, first-out, so keep the open brackets on a stack: push
on an opener, and on a closer check (and pop) the top. With a single kind of bracket the stack only ever holds `(`,
so a **counter** of open brackets can replace it.

**Which brackets are stray?** Scanning left to right, a `)` with nothing open can never be matched. After the
scan, every `(` still open can never be matched either. Removing exactly those brackets leaves a balanced string,
and no smaller removal works, because each of them is unmatched no matter what else is removed.

For `a)b(c(d)e)f)(g` the stray positions are [1, 11, 12]:

idea.md:
Scan with a stack of `(` positions: pop on a matched `)`, mark an unmatched `)` for removal. At the end,
mark every position left on the stack. Build the string without the marked positions.

lines.text: Indices of open `(`, and which positions to drop.
Each `)` closes the most recent open `(`; with none open, it's stray.
`(` still open at the end are never closed: stray.
Keep everything that isn't marked, letters included.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the stack and marks.

steps.text: Leftover '(' [12] are stray too. Remove positions [1, 11, 12]: 'ab(c(d)e)fg'.

walk.title: Push each '(' index. A ')' pops its partner, or is stray if the stack is empty. '(' left on the stack at the end are stray too.

limits.md: Stores positions; two counting passes do the same with only counters (plus the output).

idea.md:
Pass 1 (left to right): drop any `)` that arrives with no open `(`. Pass 2 (right to left over the result):
drop any `(` that arrives with no `)` to its right. What's left is balanced.

**Why two directions.** Stray `)` are detected reading forwards (nothing open yet); stray `(` are detected
reading backwards (nothing to close them).

lines.text: Left to right: a `)` with no open `(` is stray and skipped; everything else is kept. Afterwards every `)` has a partner, but some `(` may be left open.
Right to left over the kept text: a `(` with no `)` after it is an unclosed opener and is skipped.

notes.c: Written backwards into the same buffer from its end, so kept characters end up in order at the back of the buffer.
Slide the kept block to the front and terminate it.

steps.text: After pass 1 (stray ')' removed): 'ab(c(d)e)f(g', with 1 '(' still open.
After pass 2 (unclosed '(' removed from the right): 'ab(c(d)e)fg'.

walk.title: Pass 1 (left to right) drops ')' that have no open '('. Pass 2 (right to left) drops '(' that have no ')' after them.

takeaways.md:
- **Minimum removals to balance:** remove unmatched `)` (forward) and unmatched `(` (backward or leftover stack).
- A stack of positions tells you exactly which brackets to drop.
- **Pitfall:** removing letters, or removing a matched bracket.
